title: Meta Faces Big Tobacco Moment in Youth Harm Trial Brought by AGs
summary: The company risks a huge monetary penalty and forced product changes

title: JD.com Logs First Sales Fall in Latest Sign of Consumer Malaise
summary: JD.com Inc. posted its first quarterly revenue decline since listing in 2014, in the latest sign of waning Chinese consumer sentiment.

title: Workers Don Motion Trackers, Cameras to Teach AI Their Jobs
summary: They are providing robots valuable data on the very essence of human movement.

title: China’s Didi Returns to Profit on Strong Domestic Ride Demand
summary: Didi Global Inc. swung back to profit after two consecutive quarterly losses, helped by strong ride-hailing demand in China.

title: Is India’s AI Power Play Grid Locked?
summary:
AI is hungry for power, putting pressure on energy grids. Can India build a system resilient enough to keep up with its ambitious AI goals?

Tata Power CEO Praveer Sinha joins Bloomberg’s Menaka Doshi on Emerging to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Citigroup Sees Robust ADR Pipeline in Asia on Tech Funding Drive
summary: Citigroup Inc. sees more Asian companies selling shares in the US as technology firms look to raise valuations and tap the deep pools of capital in the world’s largest equity market.

title: Meta Says It’s Shut Down 750,000 Youth Accounts in Australia
summary: Meta Platforms Inc. says it has removed access to more than 750,000 Instagram and Facebook accounts in Australia believed to belong to people under 16 since it began complying with the country’s landmark youth social media ban last year.

title: Anthropic Eyes $6 Billion Offer For AI Startup Decart
summary: Anthropic is in talks to buy the AI startup Decart, according to people familiar with the matter. Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Analyst Matthew Bloxham explains that Decart's so-called world models could reduce the cost of training AI by making chips more effective and that the deal could provide an important boost to Anthropic's growth. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Trade Enforcers Deploy AI to Crack Down on Tariff Dodging
summary: The Trump administration is developing an AI-powered “detective border” to crack down on trading partners suspected of enabling China to skirt tariffs on US imports.

title: M&G Eyes Broader Opportunities Amid Concentration Risk
summary: Fabiana Fedeli, CIO of multi-asset at M&G Investments, says the level of concentration in Asian equity indices and the S&P is a concern, but that there are "plenty of opportunities" from a broader market perspective. "There are some real outstanding winners that are not actually in AI," Fedeli tells Bloomberg Television. "There's a lot of comfort that you can actually grow from that." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Cerebras Shares Tumble After Growth Underwhelms Investors
summary: Cerebras Systems Inc. slid in premarket trading after it projected slower growth than some investors anticipated, a sign the company is still in the early stages of popularizing a novel chip design.

title: CXMT Overtakes Tencent to Become Most Valuable Chinese Company
summary: CXMT Corp. has overtaken Hong Kong-listed Tencent Holdings Ltd. as the world’s most valuable Chinese company, underscoring the AI‑driven frenzy fueling demand for memory‑chip stocks.

title: Can India Meet AI’s Power Demands? | Emerging
summary: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming a new layer of strategic infrastructure, but it's hungry for power. In this episode of Emerging, Bloomberg's Menaka Doshi explores how the AI boom is reshaping electricity demand and whether it could strain power grids already challenged by rising temperatures and rapid economic growth. Featuring Tata Power CEO Praveer Sinha and Mohit Bhargava of the India Energy & Climate Center, the conversation examines whether India can generate enough power for the AI era. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: YMTC Passes Kioxia in Flash Memory Shipments, Report Says
summary: China’s Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. edged out Japan’s Kioxia Holdings Corp. in flash memory shipments during the June quarter, a sign that Chinese chipmakers are benefiting from AI-driven shortages.

title: Can India Power the AI Boom?
summary: As AI adoption accelerates, India could see a sharp increase in power demand from data centers. On the Emerging podcast, Tata Power CEO Praveer Sinha and India Energy & Climate Center's Mohit Bhargava discuss whether India is in for a grid shock.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Flipkart Founder’s Navi Said to Hire Banks for $315 Million IPO
summary: Fintech startup Navi Ltd. is preparing to formally kick off the process for an initial public offering in India, seeking to raise as much as 30 billion rupees ($314 million), according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Treasury Wine Sees Price Stabilization in China
summary: Treasury Wine Estates CEO Sam Fisher, says demand for key brands is improving after the company reported a 36% decline in annual earnings. He adds, efforts to tackle US supply chain issues and curb parallel imports in China are beginning to show results.​ He spoke exclusively with Paul Allen on Insight with Haslinda Amin. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: ASUS Lifts AI Server Growth Target
summary: ASUS Co-CEO, S.Y. Hsu, says AI server demand remains strong, prompting the company to raise its 2026 growth outlook. He discusses AI infrastructure spending, memory shortages, supply chain challenges, and the outlook for AI servers and PCs. He spoke exclusively with Paul Allen on Insight with Haslinda Amin. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Anthropic Said in Talks to Buy Startup Decart for $6 Billion
summary: Anthropic PBC is in talks to buy the artificial intelligence startup Decart AI for about $6 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Fed Rate-Hike Bets Ease on Tame CPI; Tech Shares Rally | The Asia Trade 8/13/2026
summary:
"Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" brings you everything you need to know to get ahead as the trading day begins in Asia. Bloomberg TV is live from Tokyo and Sydney with Shery Ahn and Haidi Stroud-Watts, getting insight and analysis from newsmakers and industry leaders on the biggest stories shaping global markets.
 (Source: Bloomberg)
